extracted.intended_audience: general readers; educators and social commentators interested in rural education and civic life (early 20th-century France)
extracted.subtask_description: Prescriptive commentary on what and how peasants should be taught (literacy, numeracy, hygiene, morality) and on the limits/harms of overambitious or partisan schooling; also anecdotal lessons about popular politics and electoral practice in rural France.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid partisan bias in history instruction
rubrics_metrics.description: Teaching that is strongly partisan (e.g., persuading children that the pre-Revolution period was 'barbarie, d'obscurantisme et de souffrance') fails: surveys show laïc teaching with heavy partisanship leaves students ignorant of key historical facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: the rural postman (age ~26) could not identify the 10 août (10 August 1792) or answer questions on the Revolution, knowing only vague facts about Bonaparte. The text argues that partisan civic books produce 'calembredaines' that do not stick and therefore are ineffective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize basic practical skills for rural pupils
rubrics_metrics.description: "Le bon sens et l'expérience commanderaient d'apprendre seulement au paysan à lire, à écrire, à calculer. Avec quelques notions de la géographie de son pays et quelques préceptes d'hygiène, c'est tout ce qu'il lui faudrait."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Curriculum for peasants should focus on literacy, numeracy, local geography and hygiene rather than extensive abstract or theoretical studies; the author suggests these essentials suffice for rural life and production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include moral instruction (but debate over who should teach it)
rubrics_metrics.description: The author states: "Il y aurait aussi la morale, et ce devrait être l'affaire du curé. Mais nos dirigeants éclairés ne veulent pas du prêtre. Et pourtant, quelle faillite encore que celle de la morale laïque!"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moral education is viewed as necessary to elevate souls; the text records a tension between clerical moral instruction and secular leaders who exclude the priest, leading (in the author's view) to moral failure of laïc instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid overloading with varied sciences that won't be retained
rubrics_metrics.description: Warning that by 'matagrabolisant la cervelle de sciences variées' one makes peasants suffer at school and that 'Un sur cent garde quelque chose de cette culture sottement intensive. Les autres oublient tout dès qu'ils ne sont plus sous la férule du pédagogue.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern: intensive, broad, and abstract cultural instruction that is irrelevant to pupils' lives results in poor retention and needless hardship; favor limited, relevant content to maximize lasting benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design adult/worker education mindful of time and fatigue
rubrics_metrics.description: Illustrated by the postman's reply: he has no time to read; "Toute la journée je trime sur la route et, le soir, je suis si fatigué que je m'endors aussitôt que j'ai soupé. Des fois, les jours de repos, je vais au café faire une manille." He prefers sleep or games to evening civic reading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not expect overworked adults or laborers to devote scarce leisure to dense civic or historical study; educational offerings for such populations must respect their tiredness and practical constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect vocational fit and natural aptitudes in education
rubrics_metrics.description: Quoting Ben Jonson: 'Every man in his humour... chacun dans son caractère, chacun à sa place.' The author criticizes democracy for inculcating in everyone the idea they might abandon the place assigned by heredity and faculties, producing misfits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Education should not indiscriminately encourage social mobility irrespective of aptitude; pushing all individuals toward roles unsuited to them can depopulate and despoil rural production as youth abandon the land for cities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heed local political realities and advice when campaigning
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical campaign advice implied by anecdotes: advisers warned Renaud that 'les catholiques étaient fort divisés' and that it would be difficult to unite them; he ignored such counsel to his detriment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Candidates should learn local factional lines, listen to experienced local actors, and not presume a one-size-fits-all plan; ignoring local political advice is an anti-pattern that harms electability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expect and plan for transactional electoral practices in rural areas
rubrics_metrics.description: The text documents open vote-selling and quid-pro-quo behaviour: lists of feudataires offered 'à trente sous l'une', villages asking for 4,000 francs for a promise to vote, payment to mayors for their 'due', staged demonstrations costing ten francs, free wine at meetings, and venality among electors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical guidance for actors: be prepared to negotiate, to satisfy concrete local demands (financial or infrastructural), and to budget for customary expenses of campaigning. The narrative treats this as a customary, even accepted, mode of rural electoral life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't attempt insincere public rebranding of political identity
rubrics_metrics.description: Renaud attempted a 'distinguo' by saying he contained both a Parisian royalist and a 'représentant de la catholicité mondiale', hoping to placate different groups; voters found this unconvincing and many abstained or cast blank votes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Candidates who make perfunctory or obviously opportunistic shifts in declared loyalty risk alienating both former allies and potential new supporters; authenticity and credible commitments matter to voters.
